<!-- pr-reviewer: 67eeb4c6d61d9e3d51157f76d415588e77322c82 -->
**Needs changes before merge.**

Reviewed at the safety tier (P1, wrong posted G-code). The fix is correct on all three post paths. Two items stop the merge: the per-mount and per-operation refusals have no pinning test, and a default file that holds `{}` still posts the wrong program of the issue.

### What looks good

- `posted_machine_for` is the one door from a mount to the engine. The three `engine::run_program_with` calls in `crates/app/src` use it: `posting.rs:727` (single file, also `post_setup_unwritten`), `posting_mounts.rs:336` (per mount), `posting_per_op.rs:216` (per operation).
- A refusal on a later mount or a later operation writes no file. All files are held in memory, and `write_all` writes them only after the loop. The probes below show this.
- A mounted machine does not read the default file. A document with a mounted machine still posts when the default file is missing or malformed (no false refusal).
- The refusal names the file and tells the user what to do. The text is plain English. There is no `unwrap()`, `expect()` or `panic!` in the new code in `src`.
- `engine::run` with `Value::Null` stays only in `commands/post.rs:51` (a script check, the output is discarded) and in the `post` binary of `camcraft-post` (no `--machine` argument). Neither one is a document post.
- The decision file, the `Changelog:` line and `Fixes #2319` are present. The commit subject is conventional. The diff has no CR bytes.

### Results (locally, PR head trial-merged with `origin/main` 3c7385fba: already up to date)

| Suite (`camcraft-app`) | Result |
|---|---|
| `default_machine_missing` | 3 passed |
| `posting` | 17 passed |
| `per_op_files` | 9 passed |
| `per_op_script_options` | 2 passed |
| `setup_mounts_post` | 8 passed |
| `golden_cl` | 33 passed |
| `post_not_judged` | 4 passed |
| `shipped_from_disk` | 3 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Probes (throwaway, not committed)

Each probe copies `camcraft-cli` beside a hand-made `assets/` folder and runs `process`, as `default_machine_missing.rs` does.

| Default file | Document | Result |
|---|---|---|
| missing / malformed | per mount: Setup1 mounted, Setup2 not mounted | exit 1, names `Setup2` and the file, no file written |
| missing / malformed | one file per operation, Face1 mounted, Face2 not | exit 1, names `Face2` and the file, no file written |
| missing / malformed | setup with a mounted machine | exit 0, `O0001 (Bench mill)`: correct |
| `[]`, `"x"`, `null`, empty file | not mounted | exit 1, "not a machine object" or the parse error |
| **`{}`** | not mounted | **exit 0, `O0001 (CAMCRAFT)`, no `M8` / `M9`** |
| object with no coolants | not mounted | exit 0, no `M8` / `M9` (a legal machine with no coolant) |
| object with zero spindle max and zero rapids | not mounted | exit 0, posts |

### Mutations

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| `posted_machine_for` gives `Ok(default_machine())` on error | `default_machine_missing`: 2 failed. Pinned. |
| The parse-error branch of `parse_default_machine` gives `Ok(Value::Null)` | `default_machine_missing`: 1 failed. Pinned. |
| Only `post_each` reads `machine_value_for` again | all suites pass. The per-mount probe writes `O0001 (CAMCRAFT)` with no coolant words. **Not pinned.** |
| Only the per-operation post reads `machine_value_of` again | all suites pass. The per-operation probe writes `O0002 (CAMCRAFT)`. **Not pinned.** |

### Requested before merge

1. **Pin the per-mount and per-operation refusals.** `crates/app/src/posting_mounts.rs:336` and `crates/app/src/posting_per_op.rs:216` can go back to the null machine and no test fails (mutations above). Add two tests to `crates/app/tests/default_machine_missing.rs`, with the same CLI install:
   - a document with two setups, the first with a mounted machine and the second without (one file per mount);
   - the same document with `PostOptions { per_op: true, .. }` (one file per operation).
   
   With the file missing, each must exit 1, name the file, and leave no file in the output folder.
2. **Refuse a default file that is a JSON object but not a machine.** With `{}`, `crates/app/src/posting.rs:196` (`parse_default_machine`) accepts the file. The post then writes the same wrong program that the issue reports: header `(CAMCRAFT)`, no `M8` / `M9`, exit 0. Refuse an object that has no `name` or no `kinematics.static` (the keys that the post reads for the header and the coolants). This is not the full schema check that the decision file drops. Add a test for `{}` and update the decision file.

### Notes (not blocking)

- **The refusal is kept until restart.** `default_machine_checked` (`posting.rs:181`) and `DEFAULT_TEXT` (`posting_files.rs`) keep the first result for the life of the process. If the user repairs the file while the app runs, the post continues to refuse. The text says "reinstall the file". Add "then restart CamCraft", or do not keep an `Err` in the cell. The other direction is safe: a file that breaks after a good read continues to post with the good values.
- **`default_machine()` keeps `Value::Null` for one reader**: `crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell.rs:912` (`sim::Traverse::from_machine`). It only times rapids and writes no G-code. This is acceptable.
- **The default machine's limits are not judged for a document with no mount.** The probe with a zero spindle maximum posts with exit 0. The program gate reads `Option<Machine>`, which is `None` without a mount. This is older than this PR. A follow-up issue (P7, or a defect if the shipped values must be judged) can decide it.
- **400-line rule.** `crates/app/src/posting.rs` was 1547 lines and is 1570 lines now. The growth is small and the split is not part of a P1 fix. Please file a follow-up issue to split `posting.rs` along its domain seams.
- `parse_default_machine` is `pub` and has no unit test for the non-object branch. A unit test of `parse_default_machine(Ok("[]"))` and `parse_default_machine(Ok("{}"))` is cheaper than a CLI spawn.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Review fixes are on head `4b9f7c969aa08aeefdc58430740f775b535d80c9`. The PR stays a draft.

1. The per-mount and per-operation refusals have pinning tests now. Each test reverts by mutation (see the table in the PR body).
2. `parse_default_machine` refuses an object with no `name` or no `kinematics.static` object. `{}` has a CLI test and a unit test. The shipped `3axis-vmc.mch` is the only default file, and it is accepted.

Notes:
- A refusal is not kept until restart. A failed read is read again at the next post.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 4b9f7c969aa08aeefdc58430740f775b535d80c9 -->
**Needs changes before merge.** The two blockers of the last review are fixed. One new item: the cache keeps a refused file, and the decision file says that it does not.

This is a re-review of the delta since `67eeb4c` (one commit, `4b9f7c969`), and of its effect.

### What looks good
- The per-mount and per-operation refusals are now pinned. Each test has a mounted Setup1 and an unmounted Setup2. Each test checks exit 1, the name of the file, the name of the setup or operation, and an empty output folder.
- `parse_default_machine` refuses `{}`, a blank `name`, and a missing or non-object `kinematics.static`. The unit table covers each case and the unreadable case.
- The shipped `assets/machines/3axis-vmc.mch` passes the new check (`name` "VMC 3-AXIS", `kinematics.static` is an object). It is the only copy in the tree. The wasm `include_str!` reads the same file, so no platform gets a different file.
- The new module has a provenance line and stays in `app`, next to the asset lookup. `posting.rs` is 1535 lines, smaller than before the PR. The split is follow-up #2322, and #2321 records the default limits.
- No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` in the new source.

### Results (merged with main, locally)
The trial merge with `origin/main` (`3c7385fba`) is "Already up to date". The diff has no CR bytes.

| Suite (`camcraft-app`) | Result |
|---|---|
| `default_machine_missing` | 8 passed |
| `posting` | 17 passed |
| `per_op_files` | 9 passed |
| `per_op_script_options` | 2 passed |
| `setup_mounts_post` | 8 passed |
| `golden_cl` | 33 passed |
| `post_not_judged` | 4 passed |
| `shipped_from_disk` | 3 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

Mutations (each restored after the run):
- The `post_each` site reads `machine_value_for` again: `a_missing_default_machine_file_refuses_the_post_per_mount` fails.
- The per-operation site reads `machine_value_of` again: `a_missing_default_machine_file_refuses_the_post_per_operation` fails.
- `parse_default_machine` accepts any JSON object: `an_empty_object_as_default_machine_file_refuses_the_post` and `the_default_machine_file_must_be_a_machine_object` fail.

Probes (throwaway tests, not committed):
- A mounted document with no default machine file posts: exit 0, header `O0001 (Bench mill)`.
- Cache, in one process, file at the exe's `assets/machines`:

| Sequence | Result |
|---|---|
| missing, then `{}` written, then the good file written | Err, Err, **Err** (still "it has no machine name") |
| missing, then the good file written, then `{}`, then deleted | Err, Ok, Ok, Ok (the good value stays) |
| 16 threads read a good file at the same time | 16 Ok, no panic |

The second row is safe. The kept value is the correct shipped machine, so no wrong program is posted. A repair after a missing file also works.

### Requested before merge
1. `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs:215-220` keeps the text of each file that reads, also a file that `parse_default_machine` then refuses. A repaired file is therefore not read again until a restart (row 1 above). This contradicts `docs/decisions/2319-default-machine-refusal.md:25-28` ("A failed read or a refused file is not kept: the next post reads the file again") and the PR body. The refusal text "reinstall the file" is then not true without a restart. The direction is safe, but the decision record must be true. Use one of these fixes:
   - Preferred: keep the text only when the parse is good. For example, `default_mch_text` does not cache, and `default_machine_checked` keeps only the parsed `Value` (it does that already at `posting_default_machine.rs:28`). Add a test that writes `{}`, then the good file, and expects Ok on the second call. The exe-dir lookup (`target/debug/deps/assets/machines`) lets one in-process test do this.
   - Or: change the decision file, the PR body and the advice text to say that a repair needs a restart. The decision file lists this option at line 49.

### Notes (not blocking)
- `shipped_from_disk.rs:25` is the only other caller of `default_mch_text`. A change to its cache does not touch other code.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

The re-review fix is on head `84c5a8b098f22c200f0fc03c7924ff3d7a6e8e63`. The PR stays a draft.

- `default_mch_text` reads the file at each call and keeps nothing.
- `posting::KeptMachine` keeps only a machine that passed `parse_default_machine`. A failed read or a refused text is read again at the next call.
- New test `a_repaired_default_machine_file_is_read_again_and_a_good_one_is_kept`: missing, then `{}`, then the good file give Err, Err, Ok. A later `{}` gives the kept machine.
- Mutation: the old caching (keep the text as soon as it reads) makes the new test fail at the good file.
- Green: `default_machine_missing` (9), `posting` (17), `per_op_files` (9), `setup_mounts_post` (8), `shipped_from_disk` (3). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

<!-- pr-reviewer: 84c5a8b098f22c200f0fc03c7924ff3d7a6e8e63 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** The cache blocker of the last review is fixed. A repaired default machine file now posts without a restart. This review covers the delta since `4b9f7c969` (one commit, `84c5a8b09`, 5 files, no CR bytes).

### What looks good
- `default_mch_text` reads the file at each call and keeps nothing. `KeptMachine` keeps a machine only after `parse_default_machine` accepts it.
- The decision file (`docs/decisions/2319-default-machine-refusal.md:25-30`) now agrees with the code.
- `KeptMachine` is a `OnceLock<Value>`. It has no `Mutex`, so no lock can be poisoned or held. The `get_or_init` closure only returns a value that is already parsed, so it cannot panic or call itself. When two first reads race, each one reads and checks the file, and the first value is kept. There is no `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic!` in the delta.

### Results (merged with main `677d48b46`, locally)
The trial merge is clean. Main changes 11 files, and none of them calls `machine_value*`, `default_machine*` or `default_mch_text`.

| Suite (`camcraft-app`) | Result |
|---|---|
| `default_machine_missing` | 9 passed |
| `posting` | 17 passed |
| `per_op_files` | 9 passed |
| `setup_mounts_post` | 8 passed |
| `shipped_from_disk` | 3 passed |
| `golden_cl` | 33 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

Probe through the real path (`default_machine_checked`, the file at the test exe's `assets/machines`; a throwaway test, not committed):

| Step | PR code | With the old text cache put back |
|---|---|---|
| 1. file missing | Err (cannot be read) | Err |
| 2. `{}` written | Err (no machine name) | Err |
| 3. good file written | **Ok** "VMC 3-AXIS" | Err |
| 4. `{}` written again | Ok (kept machine) | Err |
| 5. file deleted | Ok (kept machine) | Err |

- Concurrency: 32 threads started together on the first read gave 32 Ok, all the same value, and no panic.
- Mutation: `get_or_read` with no keep (it reads at each call) makes `a_repaired_default_machine_file_is_read_again_and_a_good_one_is_kept` fail.

Who reads the default machine, and how often:
- The three post paths read `posted_machine_for` -> `default_machine_checked`, once for each post, mount or operation.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/shell.rs:912` (`sim_script`) reads `posting::machine_value` -> `default_machine` only for the traverse clock. Its only caller in the app is `cached_script` (`shell.rs:900`), which runs once for each `doc_version` change and not for each frame. The tests at `tests.rs:4325` and `tests.rs:4377` also call it.
- With a good file, the machine is kept after the first read, and no call reads the disk again. With a missing or refused file, each document edit reads the file one time and writes one `tracing::error` line. This is not per frame, and the refusal stays visible.
- No other caller of `default_mch_text` exists in `crates/` (`shipped_from_disk.rs:25` is a test).

### Requested before merge
None.

### Notes (not blocking)
1. The new test drives `KeptMachine` through an injected reader. It does not pin `default_mch_text` itself. When I put the old text cache back into `default_mch_text` (`posting_files.rs:215`), all 9 tests still pass, and the real path gives Err at step 3 again. The bad direction is safe (a refusal until a restart), so this is a test gap and not a blocker. A small follow-up test can pin it. For example, add a `#[cfg(test)]` unit test in `posting_files.rs` that writes the file twice through the run-time lookup. Do not write into `target/debug/deps/assets` from a shared test, because other test binaries in that folder would then read it first. I recommend a `P7` issue for this.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
